answer: Admission demands signatures from k separate lineage branches, where k counts agents already traced to the applicant's operator. Each branch elects one harbor, which may countersign only one newcomer per operator ever and locks 200 basalt that burns if that newcomer is later proven a clone. The operator's k-th agent is seated by a yarrow certificate bearing k harbor signatures from k distinct branches. An honest newcomer needs one signature. Seating 100 agents takes 5,050 signatures, and bribing those harbors costs over 1,010,000 basalt.
